title: Automated multi-region failover drills for Private (VPC) deployments
creator: Ava Kim
description: Goal: Build a repeatable, automated failover drill flow for Redwood Private (VPC) deployments that validates multi-region readiness, upgrades, and health-check behavior. The automation should use Terraform/IaC modules, integrated health checks and observability hooks, and an executable drill runner that can be triggered by SRE or run on a schedule. The outcome should be a documented drill (runbook + playbook), Terraform modules for region orchestration, an orchestration script (CI job / Lambda / runner) that executes the drill steps, and post-drill reporting including SLO/RTO/RPO metrics.
acceptance_criteria: Provisioning: Terraform modules can create and destroy passive region resources using the same IaC (no manual steps)
Drill execution: A single command (or CI job) executes a failover drill that simulates primary-region outage and promotes the secondary region for ingress
Time objectives: End-to-end drill (start to validated failover) completes within 15 minutes in 90% of runs
Data consistency: KV cache warm-up and prefix cache behavior validated post-failover; no more than 2% user-visible errors in synthetic traffic tests
Rollback: Drill automation cleanly rolls back to original topology without manual state-massaging
Observability: Drill emits events to Console (drill:start, drill:failover, drill:completed) and uploads a run artifact (logs, metrics snapshot) to the DR dashboard
Safety: All production customer traffic is preserved unless the drill is explicitly run in maintenance mode; all destructive steps require an explicit confirmation flag in CI runner
approach_summary: We will extend the existing private-deploy Terraform modules with region-aware constructs: region module wrapper + cross-region state configuration and a lightweight promotion module. Implement a drill runner (Python) that sequences: snapshot health checks, pause primary ingress (simulate outage via route-table/ALB move or DNS weighted change), promote passive region, run synthetic traffic checks, capture metrics, and optionally perform an in-place upgrade verification. Leverage CI (GitHub Actions) to run non-destructive rehearsals and a separate runner for destructive drills that require human confirmation.
high_level_tasks: Create terraform modules: region-orchestration, promotion, and passive-validation
Design cross-region remote state pattern and locking for coordinated apply
Build drill-runner CLI (python) that invokes Terraform + healthcheck hooks
Integrate synthetic traffic harness and KV-cache warmers
Hook Console events/metrics export for drill telemetry
Document runbook and rollback playbook; add to internal DR playbook repository
Run three staged drills: non-destructive rehearsal, controlled destructive failover in staging, destructive in limited production with on-call present
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Terraform remote state conflicts during simultaneous regional applies. Mitigation: Implement a coordinator lock and use serial promotion steps in the runner.

Risk: DNS-based failover propagation delays cause long RTO. Mitigation: Prefer VPC route-table / private ALB reconfiguration for deterministic cutover in supported clouds; create DNS TTL guidelines and use health checks for automatic failover only where latency permits.

Risk: On-prem and cloud differences. Mitigation: Provide extensible adapter hooks in terraform modules so different infra teams can implement adapter scripts for BGP, MetalLB, or cloud network constructs.

Risk: Data plane divergence for stateful workloads (KV cache). Mitigation: Include cache warmers and acceptance tests that validate stateful consistency after promotion; if necessary, implement read-replica promotion steps.
Risk: Human error during destructive drills. Mitigation: Two-step confirmations, pre-check automation, and a fast rollback path in the runner.
runbook_steps: Pre-checks: verify remote state lock is free, ensure monitored metrics are within baseline, notify on-call and runbook channel
Prepare passive region: run terraform apply --target=module.passive_region to ensure resources exist
Snapshot health: run healthcheck suite against primary and passive (latency, error-rate, kv-hit-ratio)
Simulate outage: either withdraw primary route via route-table change or set primary ALB to draining; if DNS failover used then update weighted record with failover TTL and set weight 0 for primary
Promote passive: run terraform apply --target=module.promote && run promotion hooks (k8s leader election lead, promote DB replica if configured)
Verify: run synthetic traffic for 5 minutes, validate Console metrics (token latency, 5xx rate) and run KV warmers
Collect artifacts: upload logs, terraform plan/apply output, and metrics snapshot to DR dashboard and attach to the ticket
Rollback/cleanup: if drill is successful and is a rehearsal, revert DNS/route-table to original; run terraform apply to reconcile state
Postmortem: capture findings, update runbook and modules with lessons learned
test_plan: Unit tests for terraform modules using terratest or kitchen-terraform
Integration testing in staging: end-to-end drill with synthetic traffic and runbook timing
Chaos rehearsal: run non-destructive interference (packet loss / latency injection) while stepping through promotion to validate graceful degradation
Canary production drill: run in low-traffic window with on-call and rollback ready
